methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Gleb Tsipursky | Virginia’s AI training needs a first job at the other end - Augusta Free Press
signals.signal_reading: Opinion piece highlighting the structural mismatch between AI training programs and actual job availability suggests neither depth nor distribution is materializing—training without employment pathways leads to shallow adoption at best.

signals.title: Amazon bows to local backlash over AI data centers, scraps plans to build four new facilities in Northern Virginia — site to be repurposed for mixed-use and residential development. - Tom's Hardware
signals.signal_reading: Amazon scrapping four data centers due to local backlash reveals NoVA's concentration dynamics: the region has sufficient AI infrastructure density that community resistance can meaningfully constrain expansion, a luxury rural Virginia lacks.

signals.title: Roanoke coalition names Texas firm to study AI center plan - Virginia Business
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke coalition hiring consultants to study an AI Center of Excellence signals intentional capacity-building outside traditional tech hubs—if executed with depth rather than performative branding, this could distribute genuine capability westward.

signals.title: Virginia governor orders statewide plan to address AI cyberattacks - StateScoop
signals.signal_reading: Governor's executive order on AI cybersecurity represents top-down policy concentration in Richmond without evidence of distributed implementation capacity across regions—reinforcing where expertise already exists rather than building it outward.

signals.title: Roanoke County Schools opens new career and technology center - WSLS
signals.signal_reading: New career and technology center opening in Roanoke County suggests platform-delivered tech education reaching beyond NoVA, but without details on AI depth versus general digital literacy, likely signals broad-but-shallow distribution.
